newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian commodity board restructures, new posts.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian commodity board restructures, new posts.

text.p: Ivory Coast's commodities marketing board has appointed new staff to key positions and created eight new posts covering exports, quality, processing and auditing, Caistab and donor sources said on Tuesday.
"There is a new export department," said one source. "There could be more changes (other than restructuring) but we will just have to wait and see."
The changes were discussed last week with donors visiting Ivory Coast for talks on agricultural reforms linked to a $150 million World Bank loan. The talks end on May 9.
A copy of the Caistab's new structure, obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, shows a wide-ranging review of functions.
The setting up of a quality department follows industry buyers' concerns over cocoa and coffee quality after a recent liberalistion of internal marketing.

Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said in February that the Caistab might take a greater role in quality assurance in the future. Up-country quality checks were dropped by the Caistab in favour of port checks in the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) season.

The announcement of a factories department follows a recent spate of plans by investors to build cocoa factories -- in line with Ivory Coast's policy of processing up to 50 percent of its annual cocoa bean production domestically by 2000.
The talks follow a series of meetings since late 1996 between donors and Ivory Coast which have failed to resolve differences over rule changes for a commodity auction system set up in May 1996.
Caistab and exporter sources expect no immediate changes to auction rules. "The auction rules are not about to be changed," one Caistab source told Reuters.
One donor at the talks said other changes to the Caistab could be agreed this month. "We will have to wait and see... The talks are wide-ranging and the staff changes are only one part."
